Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-i9lsncbm/call-b1bf5c6669f44e2ba8e849177599515e/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for module in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    print(module, bool(importlib.util.find_spec(module)))
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
Path('tmp/pdfs').mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
with open('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt','w') as f:
    for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
        f.write(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n')
        f.write(p.extract_text() or '')
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()[:28000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
with open('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt','w',encoding='utf-8',errors='replace') as f:
    for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
        f.write(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n')
        f.write(p.extract_text() or '')
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()[:40000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'

print('ViT-L/14 Rank-1 gain over feature averaging:', round(45.913-32.016,3))

print('ViT-L/14 Rank-1 gain from adding text supervision to visual supervision:', round(45.913-43.960,3))
for name in ['manuscript.txt']+[f'page-{i:02d}.png' for i in range(1,13)]:
    (Path('tmp/pdfs')/name).unlink(missing_ok=True)
PY"

strengths: The task addresses a meaningful retrieval setting: combining a reference person image with a description of changed appearance. The zero-shot formulation sensibly avoids CPR training triplets while allowing existing person image–text supervision.

ITCPR is a potentially useful community resource, with 2,202 queries and a 20,510-image gallery drawn from three datasets. Pairing identities across clothing changes and annotating changed attributes provides a concrete benchmark for multimodal person retrieval.

The reported improvements over simple fusion are substantial. With ViT-L/14, Word4Per achieves 45.913% Rank-1 and 55.630% mAP, versus 32.016% and 41.831% for image–text averaging using the same fine-tuned encoders.

The two-stage framework is understandable and computationally practical. Training settings and runtime measurements are provided, alongside extensive ablations covering supervision, architecture, data volume, prompts, token length, and ensembles.
weaknesses: The central comparison with prior methods is not adequately controlled. Table I and Section V-B reuse Pic2Word and SEARLE inversion networks trained with original CLIP parameters alongside fine-tuned encoders, introducing a representation mismatch explicitly acknowledged in the caption. Retraining these baselines with the same encoders and person-domain data is necessary to distinguish methodological gains from domain adaptation. This substantially weakens the claimed superiority.

An untouched evaluation protocol is not established. ITCPR is described as exclusively for testing, yet architecture, prompt, and other configuration choices are justified using its results. No separate development split or independent final evaluation is described. Uncertainty estimates are also absent, making small ablation and ensemble differences difficult to assess.

Benchmark annotation reliability needs stronger support. The false-negative correction procedure retrieves a visual encoder's top-k candidates for manual inspection, but does not specify k or quantify remaining annotation errors. Annotator agreement and adjudication procedures are also missing. This does not substantiate the claim that false negatives have been eliminated, which matters directly for retrieval evaluation.

Algorithmic originality is modest relative to the cited literature: the framework combines established CLIP fine-tuning losses with image-to-pseudo-word inversion and additional text supervision. The benchmark is the clearest distinct contribution. Stronger controlled comparisons are therefore particularly important for establishing the method's contribution beyond adapting existing techniques.

The proposed explanation that text supervision suppresses background information remains suggestive. Figure 9 visualizes the frozen visual encoder rather than differences between inversion networks, while Figure 10 provides only a few examples. Quantitative background perturbation and attribute-preservation experiments would better support the claimed mechanism.

The manuscript motivates public-security applications and proposes releasing an identity-linked person benchmark, but does not discuss source-data redistribution permissions, privacy and consent handling, or surveillance misuse. These are relevant documentation and ethical-analysis omissions, rather than evidence of misconduct.
